newsitem.title: USA: Sept Brent extends gains in late U.S. cash trade.
newsitem.headline: Sept Brent extends gains in late U.S. cash trade.

text.p: North Sea benchmark Brent crude oil extended the day's earlier gains in late U.S. cash trading on Tuesday, traders said.
A full boat of September Brent was dealt at $18.29 a barrel, compared to a settlement of $18.22 on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE).
A series of partial September cargoes also switched hands at $18.29 and $18.30 for a total of 550 lots.
September Brent had already gained 13 cents a barrel from Monday's close of $18.09 a barrel.
A Wall Street firm was attributed with all of the buying of the September flat price in the U.S. window.
August/September Brent traded at 15.5 cents, while the September/October spread traded at minus six cents a barrel, even with a trade earlier in the day.
